chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say: Ali (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "and mention the Name of Allah in known days", said: The days of the ten.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.أَيَّامٍ مَعْدُودَاتٍ: Known days (specifically the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What are the 'known days' mentioned in the Quranic verse about mentioning God's name?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* offers a foundational Shia exegetical link between the 'known days' (ayyam ma'dudat) in Surah Al-Hajj and the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah. By attributing this interpretation to Imam Ali (AS), the text underscores the ritual significance of these days for sacrifice (qurbani) and divine remembrance, establishing a theological basis for their observance in Shia jurisprudence.
